Team —

Kickoff for a standing weekly handoff between Sales / Finance / Infra to keep sizing aligned to pipeline. Quick agenda below: 

- One-line pipeline review (deals that need dedicated capacity this quarter)
- Finance ask: committed vs. pipeline buffers and billing cadence
- Infra constraints: provisioning lead times, preferred instance types, preemption plan
- Actions and owners (reserve, pre-provision, or rely on burst)

Please review the attached deck + workbook and post any adjustments to estimates by Thursday EOD so we can lock a provisional reserve by Friday. Attachments: 2026-11-20-handoff-deck.pdf, Q4-pipeline-workbook.xlsx

Thanks — Rishi

Rishi —

Thanks for sending. High-level finance note: pipeline shows three large conversion candidates this quarter (HandyAI, AtlasHealth, and a regionally focused eComm customer). If we assume a 60% conversion to dedicated within 90 days for those, finance prefers a 10% buffer on top of the sizing in the workbook to avoid mid-month credit exposure.

Key ask: if Infra can provision within 7–10 days, we can move forward with a soft reserve and invoice on conversion; if lead time is >14 days we need to move to a firm reservation to guarantee capacity and adjust invoicing terms. See attached: finance_ask_note.txt (short rationale and proposed billing cadence).

Rishi / Laura —

From an infra standpoint: 1) standard provisioning lead time for a Dedicated pool node (A100-equivalent) is 12–18 business days if we need quota increases in cloud accounts; 2) if the deal is flexible on instance types we can populate with upcoming Ampere SKU in ~7 business days but performance/latency needs verification; 3) we can stage a small warm pool (hot cache priming) that buys 5–7 days of ramp on conversion.

Practical proposal: for deals with firm signatures inside 14 days, reserve firm capacity and kick procurement. For deals likely to convert in 30–90 days, use a soft-provision plan and pre-warm KV caches as Karthik suggests in the workbook.

Attached: instance-mapping.csv — rough mapping of deal size -> node count for common model families.

-Karthik
